text: The KLM nonlinear-sign (NS) gate flips the sign of only the two-photon amplitude (alpha_2|2> becomes -alpha_2|2>). Using ancilla photons and post-selection, its success probability is:
explanation: The heralded NS gate succeeds with probability 1/4 (Knill, Laflamme and Milburn, 2001). It is not deterministic (choice 1); 1/2 is the linear-optics Bell-measurement bound (choice 2); and 1/16 is the success probability of the KLM CZ built from two NS gates, not the NS gate itself (choice 3).
